Doleful

DOHL-ful · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Doleful is mournful; looking or sounding sad or sorrowful.

The doleful moan of the old ship's horn echoed across the harbor every foggy morning.

Worked Example

The abandoned puppy's doleful eyes, fixed on every passerby, made it impossible for shelter volunteers to walk past without stopping.

Doleful describes a quiet, visible sadness -- something you can see in an expression, hear in a tone, or sense in a mood.

How Strong Is It? — gloomy → anguished → doleful

gloomy vs. doleful

gloomy vs. doleful: A gloomy sky just means it looks like it might rain -- no real sorrow involved.

anguished vs. doleful

anguished vs. doleful: Anguished cries suggest severe, overwhelming pain, well beyond a doleful sigh.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — dol-

root — dol-: grief, pain (Latin dolor)

suffix — -ful

suffix — -ful: full of (Old English)

Put it together

Put it together: Doleful comes from Latin dolor ("grief, pain") + -ful ("full of") -- literally "full of grief," describing a visible, audible sorrow.

Word Choice

Doleful usually describes how sadness LOOKS or SOUNDS -- a face, a voice, a melody -- rather than the underlying reason for the sadness.
